title: Near-identity endomorphisms of a Noetherian local completion are automorphisms
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a nonzero commutative ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and assume $C$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $D=\widehat C=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}C/\mathfrak m^r$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], write $\iota:C\to D$ for the canonical map, and set $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mD$, the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)$. Let $h:D\to D$ be a unital ring endomorphism with $h(\mathfrak n)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ and $h(d)-d\in\mathfrak n^2$ for every $d\in D$. Then $D$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ and is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete. The induced map on $D/\mathfrak n$ is the identity, and for each integer $r\geq1$ the induced map on $\mathfrak n^r/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ is the identity. For every $r\geq1$ the induced endomorphism $h_r:D/\mathfrak n^r\to D/\mathfrak n^r$ is a ring isomorphism; their inverses commute with all quotient transition maps. The endomorphism $h$ is a ring automorphism, and, under the canonical identification $D\cong\varprojlim_{r\geq1}D/\mathfrak n^r$, its inverse is the map $(d_r)_r\mapsto(h_r^{-1}(d_r))_r$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] to $(C,\mathfrak m)$: $D$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mD$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] to $A=C$, $I=\mathfrak m$: $D$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] this means that the canonical ring map $\alpha:D\to\varprojlim_{r\ge1}D/\mathfrak n^r$, $d\mapsto(d\bmod\mathfrak n^r)_r$, is bijective.

The hypothesis $h(\mathfrak n)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ implies $h(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq\mathfrak n^r$ by expanding products and finite sums, so all quotient maps $h_r$ exist. Since $\mathfrak n^2\subseteq\mathfrak n$, $h_1$ is the identity. For $r\ge1$, an element of $\mathfrak n^r$ is a finite sum of terms $a x_1\cdots x_r$ with $a\in D$, $x_i\in\mathfrak n$. In the difference $h(a x_1\cdots x_r)-a x_1\cdots x_r$, replace the factors one at a time. The coefficient difference $h(a)-a\in\mathfrak n^2$ times $r$ factors in $\mathfrak n$ lies in $\mathfrak n^{r+2}$; each other term contains one $h(x_i)-x_i\in\mathfrak n^2$ and $r-1$ factors in $\mathfrak n$, hence lies in $\mathfrak n^{r+1}$. Additivity proves $h(z)-z\in\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ for every $z\in\mathfrak n^r$. This proves the asserted identity on every successive quotient.

proof.text: Induct on $r\ge1$ to prove $h_r$ bijective. The base $r=1$ was proved above. Assume $h_r$ bijective. If $h(x)\in\mathfrak n^{r+1}$, injectivity modulo $\mathfrak n^r$ gives $x\in\mathfrak n^r$; the preceding identity then gives $x\equiv h(x)\equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak n^{r+1}}$, proving injectivity at level $r+1$. Given $y\in D$, surjectivity at level $r$ supplies $x\in D$ with $e=y-h(x)\in\mathfrak n^r$. The preceding step gives $h(e)\equiv e\pmod{\mathfrak n^{r+1}}$, so $h(x+e)\equiv y\pmod{\mathfrak n^{r+1}}$. Thus $h_{r+1}$ is surjective as well. A bijective ring homomorphism has a ring-homomorphic inverse: apply its injectivity to the addition, multiplication and unit identities for the preimages. Therefore every $h_r$ is a ring isomorphism.

proof.text: For $s\ge r\ge1$, let $q_{s,r}:D/\mathfrak n^s\to D/\mathfrak n^r$ be reduction. On representatives $q_{s,r}h_s=h_rq_{s,r}$. Composing with the two inverses yields $q_{s,r}h_s^{-1}=h_r^{-1}q_{s,r}$. Hence $H((d_r)_r)=(h_r(d_r))_r$ and $G((d_r)_r)=(h_r^{-1}(d_r))_r$ are well-defined ring maps on the compatible-sequence ring of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $HG=GH=1$ coordinate by coordinate. The canonical bijection $\alpha$ from step 1 satisfies $\alpha h=H\alpha$, again on each coordinate. Thus $h$ is a ring automorphism with inverse $\alpha^{-1}G\alpha$, giving exactly the formula in the statement.
